title: Completion of a coordinate-ratio chart at an exceptional rational point
statement:
Let $L$ be any field, $n\ge1$, $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Choose $h\in J$, put $e=X_h$, and inside the localization $A[1/e]$ (fractions $a/e^m$, with the usual fraction operations) put
$$C=A[X_j/e:j\in J\setminus\{h\}],\qquad r_j=X_j/e.$$
For scalars $\xi_j\in L$ let $\mathfrak n=(e,X_k\ (k\notin J),r_j-\xi_j\ (j\in J\setminus\{h\}))C$. This is a maximal ideal with $C/\mathfrak n=L$. Put $B=L[[X'_1,\ldots,X'_n]]$. The continuous substitution $X_h\mapsto X'_h$, $X_j\mapsto X'_h(\xi_j+X'_j)$ for $j\in J\setminus\{h\}$, and $X_k\mapsto X'_k$ for $k\notin J$, extended by $r_j\mapsto\xi_j+X'_j$, induces an isomorphism
$$\varprojlim_{m\ge1}C/\mathfrak n^m\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ B$$
[def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It takes the completion map $C\to\varprojlim_m C/\mathfrak n^m$ to the displayed substitution on $C$, and takes $\mathfrak n$ to $(X'_1,\ldots,X'_n)$.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak a=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)A$, $\mathfrak q=(X'_1,\ldots,X'_n)B$, and $t_h=e$, $t_j=r_j-\xi_j$ for $j\in J\setminus\{h\}$, $t_k=X_k$ for $k\notin J$. Thus $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)C$. In either power-series ring, the $m$th power of the variable ideal consists exactly of series with no terms of total degree less than $m$: products of $m$ variables have this property; conversely assign each monomial of degree at least $m$ to a chosen degree-$m$ divisor, and group the remaining coefficients into one series for each of the finitely many degree-$m$ divisors. Consequently every series equals its finite truncation below degree $m$ modulo this ideal power. Also $\mathfrak aC\subseteq\mathfrak n$, since $X_j=e r_j$ for $j\in J\setminus\{h\}$ and all the other $X_i$ are among the $t_i$.

proof.text: Apply the chart-presentation statement to $R=A$, $a=e$, and the other generators $X_j$ for $j\in J\setminus\{h\}$. It presents $C$ as the image of $Q=A[Y_j]/(eY_j-X_j)$, with kernel precisely the $e$-power torsion of $Q$. The map from $Q$ to $B$ given by $\sigma$ on $A$ and $Y_j\mapsto\xi_j+X'_j$ respects the relations. Multiplication by $X'_h$ on $B$ is injective: the coefficient at $\nu+\mathbf e_h$ of $X'_hF$ is the coefficient at $\nu$ of $F$. Hence this map kills the entire $e$-power-torsion kernel, and factors through a ring map $\phi:C\to B$. It sends $r_j$ to $\xi_j+X'_j$ and each $t_i$ to $X'_i$, so $\phi(\mathfrak n^m)\subseteq\mathfrak q^m$. Denote its induced map by $\phi_m:C/\mathfrak n^m\to B/\mathfrak q^m$.

proof.text:
The composite $\phi_m\overline\psi_m$ sends a series class to its truncation below degree $m$, which is the same class by step 1. For the other composite, let $a=\sum a_
u X^
u\in A$. Step 2 computes $\sigma(a)$ modulo $\mathfrak q^m$ as a finite sum in the $b_i$. Substituting $X'_i\mapsto t_i$ in this sum sends $b_h$ to $e$, $b_j$ to $e(\xi_j+t_j)=e r_j=X_j$, and $b_k$ to $X_k$. Thus $\overline\psi_m\phi_m(a)=\sum_{|
u|<m}a_
u X^
u=a mod\mathfrak n^m$, since the omitted tail lies in $\mathfrak a^mC\subseteq\mathfrak n^m$. On $r_j$ the same composite gives $\xi_j+t_j=r_j$. Since $C$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by these $r_j$, the composite is the identity on $C/\mathfrak n^m$. This proves that the two displayed maps are inverse ring isomorphisms for every $m$.

proof.text: For $m=1$ the preceding isomorphism gives $C/\mathfrak n\cong B/\mathfrak q=L$, where the latter map is the constant coefficient: its kernel is $\mathfrak q$ by step 1. Thus $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, and the residue-field isomorphism is the identity on $L$. In particular the proposed ideal is proper, without any assumption that the scalars $\xi_j$ vanish.

proof.text: By the definition of completion, a compatible family $z_m\in C/\mathfrak n^m$ is sent coordinatewise to $(\phi_m(z_m))_m$; the inverse is coordinatewise $\overline\psi_m$. Compatibility was checked in step 4, and the inverse identities in step 5, so this gives $\widehat C\cong\varprojlim_m B/\mathfrak q^m$. The completeness of $B$, with the definition of adic completeness, identifies the latter limit with $B$. On a class coming from $c\in C$ its coordinates are $\phi(c)\bmod\mathfrak q^m$, so this isomorphism identifies the completion map with precisely $\phi$. Its inverse sends $X'_i$ to the completed image of $t_i$. The ideal generated by $\mathfrak n$ in $\widehat C$ therefore maps to $\mathfrak q$. Both maps preserve every power of these ideals, hence are continuous. For $J=\{h\}$ the lists of $r_j,Y_j,\xi_j$ are empty and the same formulas give the identity completion of $A$; for $J=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there are no unaffected variables. This covers these cases and $n=1$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q97-eab9ef6a7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 7 steps in full; there are no new nodes and no fixes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, and proof_deps is exactly the union of the step uses. Step 1 proves elementarily that the m-th power of the variable ideal is the set of series with no terms of degree below m, and that aC is contained in n. Step 2 applies lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation with T=B, I=q and b_j=X'_h(xi_j+X'_j) in q; this node is a generic tool from unit sk-thm-p1, declared in split_report.tool_uses, and I accept it. Step 3 applies lem-trf-blowup-chart-presentation-power-torsion (Stacks 0G8S, algebra.tex:17250, checked) with R=A, a=e, a_i=X_j; A[I/e]=A[X_j/e] in one line, and the map kills the e-power-torsion kernel because X'_h is a nonzerodivisor. Steps 4-5 give truncation inverses psi_m; I checked that psi(b_j)=e(xi_j+t_j)=X_j, that the tail of a lies in a^mC, contained in n^m, and that r_j is sent back to r_j, so the nonzero shift is handled explicitly. Step 6 gives C/n=L, so n is maximal. Step 7 passes to the limit using the completeness of B; the completion map goes to phi and the extended ideal of n goes to q. Edge cases checked: n=1, J={h}, J = all coordinates, xi nonzero, characteristic p. The Mathlib no-match is right: toAdicCompletionAlgEquiv (Equiv.lean:344) completes a polynomial ring only. A statement search of the DAG and blueprint_refs found no duplicate (only toric/monoid completions). The sole citer, coordinate-blowup-division-generators, uses exactly what is proved. No SGA citation; no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply.
